tasks.short: Use equipment and materials during presentations

steps.what: Set up computers, audio-visual aids and materials for the presentation
Use equipment and materials to supplement the live presentation

tasks.design: Retain physical setup and responsive classroom use of {OTHER}, the classroom presentation equipment. Prepared materials may sit in {DOCS}, but this task does not include producing them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment needs setup and adult control during a live classroom activity.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing presentation controls already support the teacher.
tasks.still_hard: The teacher must judge whether a visual or recording is helping children understand.
tasks.human_edge: Connect the equipment-supported example to the children's immediate learning.
tasks.altitude: Equipment use and classroom responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Operating aids during a live presentation retains its labour; material-drafting tools do not establish savings for this task.

assumptions: Boundary is equipment setup and use, excluding presentation creation and general instruction already assigned elsewhere. A roll-up allocates any overlapping delivery episode once.
No new structured readiness flag or automated classroom response is introduced.
Existing native presentation controls remain in use with no configuration change or incremental upkeep, justifying zero.
unknowns: Equipment reliability and available technical support
research_questions: Which equipment faults interrupt live classroom use?

already_counted.description: Physical setup and live use of presentation aids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Existing equipment runtime earns no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss pupil needs and progress with professionals

steps.what: Meet with professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress

tasks.design: Keep professional discussion and agreement with the teacher and relevant specialists. Existing pupil information in {OTHER}, the pupil record system, supports the meeting without a new recording or summary tool.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different professionals hold different observations and must interpret them together.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records already support the retained discussion.
tasks.still_hard: An apparent disagreement may reflect different settings or incomplete context.
tasks.human_edge: Explain classroom observations and integrate specialist advice into workable support.
tasks.altitude: Professional consultation duties and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Role boundaries and appropriate information sharing

evidence.claim: Professional pupil-support discussion retains all labour, without an invented meeting-administration baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is the teacher's planned professional consultation, excluding original observation, formal report writing and urgent concern escalation assigned to task 6515. The roll-up must not add the same conversation twice.
No automated step requires new pupil classifications or structured meeting outputs.
Existing native pupil-record access suffices. No new system or process maintenance is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Professional consultation arrangements and information-sharing permissions
research_questions: Can each professional explain the evidence and their agreed support responsibility?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Consultation and agreement remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach and monitor safe equipment use

steps.what: Instruct students in safe use and care of equipment and materials
Monitor equipment use and intervene to prevent injuries or damage

tasks.design: Keep safety demonstration and direct supervision with the teacher. Equipment guidance in {DOCS} supports preparation, while no monitoring model or automated intervention is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Young children need live demonstration and immediate supervision around equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing guidance already supports the retained adult responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: A child may understand an instruction and still act unsafely during play.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise danger early and intervene clearly without discouraging appropriate exploration.
tasks.altitude: Safety supervision and teaching duties remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Safe-use instruction and physical supervision retain their labour in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is equipment-specific demonstration and supervision, excluding general classroom discipline and equipment maintenance.
No new structured injury-risk flag or automated child assessment is needed.
Existing native equipment guidance is sufficient; no deployment or extra upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which equipment activities require closer adult supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. No safety instruction or observation is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Interpret curriculum guidelines and select course objectives and progression
Prepare course outlines linking objectives to units and activities

loop.purpose: Draft a course outline from teacher-selected goals and progression
loop.input: Course brief, goal descriptions and available teaching periods
loop.output: Draft units and sequence with goal and source links
loop.check: Teacher verifies actual goal coverage, suitable progression, realistic timing and developmental fit of proposed activities
loop.stop: One revision then manual planning if coverage or progression remains unsuitable
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the outline, but connecting goals to varied activities and transitions needs semantic drafting

steps.what: Check guideline coverage and approve the final course outline

tasks.design: Use a fixed curriculum-goal list and native outline templates in {DOCS}, with a bounded draft for unit sequencing and activity descriptions. The teacher decides progression and checks the final course against curriculum and school requirements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required goals must be rewritten into a coherent sequence of units and activities.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can work from explicit goals and teaching-time constraints.
tasks.still_hard: Formal coverage does not ensure an appropriate or feasible developmental progression.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a sequence that makes sense for the children rather than merely filling every goal row.
tasks.altitude: Less outline drafting; curriculum interpretation and course approval remain with the teacher.

reach.learn: Goal coverage and developmentally suitable sequencing

evidence.claim: Snappet supports drafts of classroom activities for a lesson goal; this establishes goal-based preparation assistance, not independent course planning.
Aila's English primary-school trial reduced weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours while covering 7% of lessons; this does not establish a kindergarten course-outline saving.

assumptions: Boundary is course-level objectives and outlines. Task 6508 owns lesson-specific wording and communication to children; the same objective-writing action must not be counted twice.

The teacher produces goal references, desired progression, class context, available periods and school constraints in s1, retaining all 40 hours. Missing or conflicting guidelines require manual clarification before drafting.
Test native curriculum lists and existing outline templates first. Retained s2 time includes semantic correction; s3 retains all final coverage and feasibility review.
unknowns: Available outline templates and current drafting time
research_questions: Does the reviewed outline genuinely cover the chosen goals with a workable developmental sequence?

already_counted.description: Planning brief, draft correction and final outline review

incremental.description: Maintain guideline versions and review recurring draft errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact course outline, goal links, unit sequence, timing and guideline versions; changes require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+20+20=80; gross 20%, minus four upkeep gives 16% central net. Low assumes only seven drafting hours removable because curriculum mapping and timing require more correction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce course-outline drafting while retaining classroom equipment use, safety supervision and professional pupil discussions.
reach: Coordinate course progression with early years curriculum specialists
role.ambitious_version: A kindergarten teacher who spends less time writing course outlines and retains full attention to children and colleagues.
